Subject: FintechCo - deployment mode follow-up (SSO, KMS, logging)

Hi Samir / Leah —

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to hear more about FintechCo’s production requirements. Below is a short recap + a few clarifying questions so we can scope the right deployment recommendation (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).

Recap (what we heard):
- Primary concern: regulatory controls around key management, auditability, and long-term log retention.
- SSO: you use Okta (SAML 2.0) for admin access and want SCIM provisioning for service accounts.
- KMS/HSM: you require customer-managed keys (CMK) and want HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest for any PII/PHI processed.
- Logging retention: security/legal require up to 7 years of immutable audit logs and integration with your SIEM (Splunk).

Clarifying questions:
1) For KMS/HSM: is AWS KMS with a customer-managed CMK sufficient, or do you specifically require a dedicated HSM appliance (e.g., AWS CloudHSM or on-prem HSM)?
2) For logs: do you need us to store logs for 7 years on Redwood’s side, or is long-term retention handled by pushing logs to your SIEM/cloud storage?
3) Any constraints on network connectivity (e.g., must be fully air-gapped, or can we establish VPC peering / PrivateLink)?

Initial thoughts (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to deploy but limited for customer-managed HSM and long-term immutable logging.
- Dedicated capacity: gives isolated capacity and can support BYOK (bring-your-own-key) via AWS KMS, but HSM-level integration and 7-year immutable retention usually push customers toward Private (VPC / on-prem).
- Private VPC / on-prem: most flexible for HSM, long retention, and strict networking/compliance needs.

Next steps I propose:
- Nikhil (cc’d) — can we schedule a technical deep-dive to map FintechCo’s KMS/HSM and logging architecture and confirm whether Dedicated could meet requirements or if we should scope Private?
- Samir / Leah — if you can share the security questionnaire + any architecture diagrams, that’ll speed the assessment.

I attached a short checklist to capture the integration details (SSO, KMS, logging) — filling that out will help our SE team.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

- Logs: Our legal team requires 7-year retention; we normally ingest logs into our Splunk instance. Ideally Redwood would forward audit logs to our SIEM and also support an immutable archive option.
- Network: VPC peering or PrivateLink is fine; fully air-gapped on-prem is only needed for a subset of workloads.

Hi Samir / Leah —

Thanks — I’m Nikhil, SE on Marissa’s team. Below is a concise technical recommendation and proposed action plan based on the constraints you described.

Technical summary (recommendation):
- Private VPC / on-prem: Recommended if you require HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM or customer-managed HSM), immutable 7-year archives on Redwood’s side, or strict network isolation for prod workloads. Private gives full control over networking, KMS/HSM attachments, and long-term storage configuration.
- Dedicated capacity + BYOK: Viable if you can accept AWS KMS CMK (not CloudHSM) and you will handle immutable archiving in your own S3/SIEM. We can support VPC peering/PrivateLink, SCIM/SAML for SSO, and pushing audit logs to your Splunk forwarder.

Tradeoffs:
- TIMELINE: Dedicated pilot: 2–4 weeks (provisioning + BYOK setup + log forwarding). Private pilot: 4–8 weeks (network setup, key provisioning, runbook/testing).
- COMPLEXITY: Private requires more onboarding (network, onboarding windows, potential firewall rules). It does allow for HSM appliances and more flexible long-term retention strategies.
- COST: Private has higher fixed setup cost and longer lead times for SLA/ops onboarding.

Action plan (proposed):
1) Security deep-dive (SE + your security team) — 60m to validate HSM requirement and log flows.
2) Pilot scope decision: Dedicated pilot (BYOK + Splunk forwarding) vs Private pilot (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM, immutable archive).
3) Deliverables for pilot: runbook, KMS/HSM compatibility matrix, PoC network diagram, and test-plan.

Attachments I’m including: redwood-private-deployment-runbook.pdf (runbook for Private VPC deployments), redwood-kms-hsm-compatibility-matrix.xlsx (matrix showing which models/features support BYOK vs HSM), and a suggested timeline.

Proposed times for the SE deep-dive: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:00–10:00 PT. I’ll hold those times and send invites after I hear what works for you.

If you want a short written comparison for procurement, I can convert the above into a 1-page doc for your legal/security teams.

Cheers,
Nikhil Sharma
